title: A case of anti-nephrin antibody-positive, steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome with successful discontinuation of immunosuppressants following rituximab
creator: Kota Shinzato, Norifumi Hayashi, Ryoko Akai, Yu Kagaya, Yutaka Hiratuji, Sho Kumano, Kazuaki Okino, Keiji Fujimoto, Takao Iwawaki, Kengo Furuichi
description: Minimal change nephrotic syndrome (MCNS) is a major cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and adults. Recent studies identified circulating anti-nephrin antibodies in 30%–50% of patients, linking them to severe proteinuria and frequent relapses. We describe a Japanese woman in her 40s with steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome (SDNS).

title: Acute Respiratory Failure due to Pulmonary Toxoplasmosis in an Immunocompetent Patient: A Case Report
creator: María Jesús Ojeda, María Isabel Domínguez, Leonardo Soto, Rodrigo Kemeny, Pablo Regueira, Guillermo Ávila, Tomas Regueira
description: Pulmonary toxoplasmosis is a rare but potentially life‐threatening manifestation of Toxoplasma gondii infection in immunocompetent individuals. Clinical presentation is often nonspecific and may mimic viral or atypical pneumonia, leading to delayed diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 32‐year‐old man who presented with a mononucleosis‐like syndrome complicated by rapidly progressive hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.

title: Progress and Prospects in Otorhinolaryngology—Head and Neck Surgery in Ethiopia
creator: Daniel G. Eyassu, Eliyas Asfaw, Christian Schaaff, Cody L. Messick, Assaye Nibret, Seid Temam, Nardos Getachew Bulfeta, Kassaw Ketemaw, Gebrewahd Alemu, Michael Kebede, Joshua P. Wiedermann
description: IntroductionThis paper aims to explore the current state of otorhinolaryngology—head and neck surgery (ORL‐HNS) training and practice in Ethiopia, identify major barriers to development, and also highlight the optimistic prospects for the future, with strategies to build a self‐sustaining ORL‐HNS specialty capable of meeting the growing needs of the Ethiopian population.

title: Preparation of levulinic acid and 5-(chloromethyl)furfural directly from terrestrial and marine biomass in a batch reactor under conventional and microwave heating
creator: Diona Avitha Aranha, Abhishek Kumar Yadav, Balamurugan Ayyakkalai, Vijayalekshmi Vijayakumar, Fillip Kumar Sarkar, Hemanth Giri Rao Vantharam Venkata, Sri Sailaja Nori, Saikat Dutta
description: Lignocellulosic waste and seaweed represent second- and third-generation biomass resources, respectively, with significant potential as renewable feedstocks for the sustainable production of liquid fuels and value-added organic chemicals. In this study, the production of levulinic acid (LA) and 5-(chloromethyl)furfural (CMF), two important carbohydrate-derived platform chemicals, was investigated using selected lignocellulosic wastes and dried seaweed flakes (DSF) of E. spinosum.

title: Lactate Dehydrogenase, Interleukin‐6, and 24 h Intra‐Abdominal Pressure Exhibit Early Predictive Value in Hypertriglyceridemic Pancreatitis Complicated by Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
creator: Kaiqiang Zhu, Bin Lu, Ranran Zhou, Lei Xu
description: BackgroundHypertriglyceridemia‐induced acute pancreatitis (HTG‐AP) is increasingly recognized as a major cause of acute pancreatitis in China. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), a severe and early complication, significantly worsens prognosis and increases intensive care unit (ICU) burden. This study aimed to identify early predictive markers of ARDS in patients with HTG‐AP, enabling timely risk stratification and clinical intervention to improve outcomes.

title: Unraveling the role of rare earth dopants (Ce, La, Sm, and Y) in modifying the catalytic effect of TiO2 for MgH2 dehydrogenation: a first-principles analysis
creator: Xinru Zhu, Yaru Liu, Zhaohui Huang, Lumin Wang, Ling Wang, Min Li, Zhen Li, Yuexing Zhang, Longqing Yang, Xiaoli Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Magnesium hydride (MgH2) suffers from sluggish dehydrogenation kinetics owing to its strong Mg–H bonding, which limits its practical application. In this work, we present a systematic density functional theory (DFT) and climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) study on the adsorption and dissociation behavior of MgH2 on rare-earth (RE = Ce, La, Sm, Y) doped TiO2(001) surfaces, with particular focus on the regulatory effects of doping configuration (substitutional vs. interstitial) and RE identity.

title: Study Protocol of the Endobronchial VAlves for Pneumothorax to Reduce Admission Time (EVAPoRATe) Pilot Multicentre Randomised Clinical Trial
creator: Nai‐Chien Huan, Niranjan Ananda Setty, Ai Ling Tan, Dhaval Thakkar, Taha Huseini, Elaine Yap, Jonathan Williamson, Phan Nguyen, Paul Lilburn, Matthew Salamonsen, Arash Badiei, Matthew Ing, Sanjeevan Muruganandan, Bapti Roy, Brent Gardiner, Lonny B Yarmus, Steven P Walker, Y C Gary Lee
description: BackgroundPneumothorax with persistent air leak (PAL) is a debilitating condition. Patients with PAL often require prolonged chest drainage, with associated complications, such as, hospital‐acquired infections, thromboembolism, and deconditioning. Endobronchial valves (EBVs) are an approved bronchoscopic treatment for PAL and may allow earlier chest tube removal and hospital discharge.

title: The Proctitis Paradox: Refractory Ulcerative Proctitis Associated With Development of Disease Complications in a Multicenter South Australian Cohort
creator: Sreecanth S Raja, Samuel P Costello, Alexandra Sadler, Nicholas Wan, Bhuwan Tandon, Dharshan Sathananthan, Kate D Lynch, Chris K Rayner, Suzanne Edwards, Robert V Bryant
description: BackgroundDespite limited extent, patients with ulcerative proctitis (UP) can suffer from debilitating symptoms, complications, and risk of disease extension. The aim was to provide a contemporary real‐world insight into the management and outcomes of UP.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted of UP patients attending three tertiary hospitals in Adelaide, South Australia, between 2015 and 2024.

title: Association Between the Dietary Inflammatory Index and Cardiorenal Anemia Syndrome: Evidence From NHANES and Related‐Phenotype Exploration in KNHANES
creator: Shirong Lin, Yufeng Chen, Yadan Chen, Lihan Wu, Weijia Zeng, Haiyang Song, Wenjun Ding, Xiaoxiangxin Luo, Jun Ke, Feng Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cardiorenal anemia syndrome (CRAS) links heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and anemia, but the role of diet‐related inflammation remains unclear. In the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), we examined associations of the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) with CRAS, dose–response patterns, inflammatory mediation, and machine‐learning prediction, alongside analysis of a myocardial infarction–CKD–anemia phenotype in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). This study included 25,388 NHANES and 32,935 KNHANES adults.

title: Antibiotic use in children with suspected CNS infection in the molecular diagnostic era: a cohort study of 1198 children
creator: Yannik Vollmuth, Katrin Baalmann, Jana Beer, Benjamin Soric, Uta Behrends, Melanie Meyer-Bühn, Christoph Klein, Johannes Hübner, Gerhard Dobler, Tilmann Schober
description: ObjectivesCentral nervous system (CNS) infections in children require rapid diagnostic evaluation and prompt empiric antimicrobial therapy. However, clinical presentation is often non-specific, leading to frequent use of broad-spectrum antibiotics while awaiting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) results. We evaluated antibiotic treatment modifications during the diagnostic work-up and quantified changes in antibiotic spectrum coverage (ASC) before and after lumbar puncture (LP).

title: Unveiling Particulate Matter–Lung Interactions from Static Models to Dynamic Lung-on-Chips
creator: Yixin Ren, Xi Deng, Mengqi Yang, Ziwei Liang, Yan Wei, Ting Liu, Weiwei Lan, Yiwei Shi, Di Huang
description: The pervasive inhalable particulate matter (PM) in the environment poses a marked threat to pulmonary health. However, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood, largely due to the limitations of existing in vitro models in accurately mimicking the complex biological processes.

title: Manic switching is seldom observed during rTMS therapy for unipolar depression: Implications for antidepressant mechanisms
creator: Yuki Matsuda, Shun Takahashi
description: orsolateral prefrontal cortex target defined as 5.5 cm anterior to the site used to determine the motor threshold. Stimulation was delivered at a frequency of 10 Hz and an intensity of 120% of the standard motor threshold. Each session comprised 75 trains, each lasting 4 s stimulation, yielding a total of 3000 pulses.

title: Malaria burden across 126 tropical countries and territories, 1990–2021: tropical-climate share, sociodemographic correlates, population dynamics, and projections to 2050
creator: Qiangbing Liao, Xiaoyan Zheng, Xiaoyang Zhang, Zhiwei Chen
description: BackgroundMalaria remains a major global health challenge, particularly in tropical regions. Although recent global reports describe persistent malaria burden, fewer studies have jointly assessed tropical-climate context, sociodemographic development, demographic decomposition, and future projections across tropical countries. This study aimed to provide an integrated assessment of malaria burden and its ecological correlates among tropical countries and territories.

title: Insecticide resistance in larval populations of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus from Panama
creator: Lorenzo Cáceres Carrera, Dan Martínez, Luis Piedra, Antonio Bruno, Anakena M. Castillo, Rolando Torres-Cosme
description: IntroductionThe control of Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus is the most effective strategy for preventing the transmission of the arboviruses DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV. However, insecticide resistance threatens the sustainability of vector control programs. Monitoring insecticide resistance enables the identification of potential associated factors, its intensity and distribution, and contributes to the development of more effective strategies for its management.

title: Clinical outcomes and molecular features of CEBPA-mutated MPAL: a multi-center case series
creator: Yirong Wu, Weijie Luo, Na An, Xiaohan Zhang, Jianyun Li, Yixuan Cao, Yunxin Zeng, Peng Ke, Lu Liu, Linlin Yang, Changru Luo, Shiyu Chen, Sitian Yang, Haoyu Peng, Xiaoqing Li, Jingchao Fan, Rujiao Dong, Bingbing Wen, Xin Du, Lixin Wang, Guangyang Weng
description: Mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL) is rare and aggressive, with no standard therapy. CEBPA mutations define favorable-risk AML, but their significance in MPAL is unknown. We reviewed eight CEBPA-mutated MPAL patients from five Chinese centers. Four received allo-HSCT in first complete remission and all remained alive and relapse-free (median follow-up of 24.0 months).

title: The Brucella effector protein BtpB facilitates STAT3 activation to regulate polarization in macrophages during infection
creator: Ye Yuan, Minghui Wang, Mingyue Hao, Jialu Chen, Xiaofang Liu, Yuanhao Yang, Yimeng Cui, Shengnan Li, Wei Liu, Dong Zhou, Wei Liu, Yaping Jin, Aihua Wang
description: Brucella is a Gram-negative facultative intracellular pathogen that causes widespread zoonotic infections. Macrophages are crucial immune and antigen-presenting cells that differentiate into proinflammatory M1-type or anti-inflammatory M2-type cells in different microenvironments. The BtpB protein of Brucella is a type IV secretion system effector protein that modulates host inflammatory responses by inhibiting Toll-like receptor signaling and controlling dendritic cell activation.

title: Implementation of specialised care improves survival in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
creator: Omar Keritam, Daniel Bormann, Friedrich Haimberger, Diana Gharib, Merve Sener, Felix Gruber, Lukasz Antoniewicz, Ivan Fedak, Andreas Renner, Bernhard Fasching, Sabine Ullrich, Rafael Paternostro, Werner Dolak, Eva K Masel, Othmar Schuhfried, Jakob Rath, Gudrun Zulehner, Martin Krenn, Fritz Zimprich,
description: ObjectiveAccess to multidisciplinary care influences survival in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (pwALS). However, real-world data comparing structured specialised care with general neurological management remain limited. We aimed to assess the influence of implementing a specialised outpatient clinic on survival in pwALS.

title: Duloxetine for postoperative pain management in total hip and knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Abdelrahman Ibrahim, Mohamed Abdelnabi, Reda Ali Sheta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPostoperative pain following total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) drives opioid dependence. Perioperative duloxetine is an option as a multimodal analgesic adjunct, yet its efficacy and safety in this population are not fully defined.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis compared perioperative duloxetine to placebo in THA and TKA patients, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (CRD420261294277).

title: Physician workforce imbalances in Japan: how structural incentives shape hospital-based acute-care capacity
creator: George Kujo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Japan's physician workforce problem in hospital-based high-intensity care is better understood as an interaction between distribution and retention than as a simple question of national physician headcount. This Comment examines three pathways that can reduce hospital service capacity: working conditions that impede entry and career continuity in high-intensity specialties; early movement from initial residency into cosmetic medicine, known as choku-bi; and later movement from hospital employment to clinic practice.

title: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and critical care readiness amid Afghanistan’s returnee crisis
creator: Hayatullah Takal
description: ack of funding, and the 2026 national health response remains only 17% funded [2]. This compounding emergency carries a direct, and so far unaddressed, implication for critical care. Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is endemic across the Afghanistan–Pakistan–Iran border region, and unlike many zoonoses discussed only at the public-health level, it is a genuine critical care disease.

title: Mechanism of RNA‐Binding Protein ELAVL1 in Promoting Th2 Cell Differentiation Through Stabilizing CPA3 mRNA in Allergic Rhinitis
creator: Meng‐Ya Liu, Hong‐Bing Yao, Cheng Chen
description: This study aimed to elucidate the role of the RNA‐binding protein embryonic lethality abnormal vision‐like protein 1 (ELAVL1) in the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis (AR), specifically by investigating its potential to promote T helper 2 (Th2) cell differentiation by regulating the stability of carboxypeptidase A3 (CPA3) mRNA. Differentially expressed genes associated with AR were screened via bioinformatic analysis.

title: “I Really Feel Heard by AI”: A Cultural Case Study of AI-Mediated Listening Across China and the UK
creator: Xin Zhan
description: The increasing use of generative AI for emotional support has prompted growing debate about the future of mental health care. This article suggests that such reliance is better understood not simply as a technological shift, but as symptomatic of a wider crisis in the politics of listening.

title: Reframing the epidemiological transition as increasing returns to tackling aging-related diseases
creator: Julian Ashwin, David E. Bloom, Naomi Lee, Peter Piot, Andrew J. Scott
description: Global life expectancy has risen since 1973 from 58 to over 73 years, while the share of people aged 65 years and older has doubled to 10% and is projected to reach 21% by 2073. This shift is linked to an epidemiological transition from infectious to chronic disease.

title: Histone deacetylases in cancer metabolic reprogramming
creator: Yu Hyun Jeon, Hyeyeong Seo, Ji Woo Youn, Jung Yoo, Sang Wu Lee, Soo Yeon Oh, So Hee Kwon
description: Cancer cells undergo extensive metabolic reprogramming to sustain rapid proliferation and adapt to heterogeneous tumour microenvironments. These metabolic alterations are tightly linked to epigenetic regulation, which reshapes gene expression and cellular signalling mechanisms. Among epigenetic regulators, histone deacetylases (HDACs) have emerged as key modulators of cancer metabolic reprogramming.

title: Spinal cord injury is associated with reduced cognitive capacity to self-regulate, organise and adapt to new situations
creator: Daniel Myles, Danielle Sandalic, Michael Gascoigne, Ilaria Pozzato, Mohit Arora, Candice McBain, Yvonne Tran, James W. Middleton, Ashley Craig
description: Study designCross-sectional observational cohort studyObjectivesTo investigate differences in executive function (EF) in adults with spinal cord injury (SCI) compared with able-bodied (AB) controls across tasks imposing varying levels of executive demand, and to examine implications for targeted cognitive screening.SettingTwo SCI units in New South Wales (SCI), Australia, and the community of New South Wales, Australia (able-bodied).

title: Terahertz-based prognostic framework for glioma: from spectral features to patient-level prognostic assessment
creator: Minghui Du, Rui Tao, Zhiyan Sun, Peiyuan Sun, Xianhao Wu, Yubo Wu, Tianyi Bi, Zhaohui Zhang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Dabiao Zhou, Pei Yang
description: In glioma, accurate prediction of recurrence and survival is essential for clinical decision-making and individualized management. However, current prognostic tools do not fully capture outcome heterogeneity, and convenient approaches for early postoperative prognostic evaluation are lacking. We investigated whether terahertz (THz) spectroscopy could provide label-free prognostic information.

title: Correction to: Dual Osteoprotective Actions of the Kefir Peptide KFP-1: Enhancement of Bone Formation and Suppression of Bone Resorption in Cells and Murine Models
creator: Min-Che Tung, Gary Ro-Lin Chang, Min-Yu Tu, Hueng-Chuen Fan, Chih-Ching Yen, Abdulkadir Cidem, I.-Chien Chen, Chuan-Mu Chen
description: published in the wrong order. Specifically, the image intended for Figure 1 appeared as Figure 8, while the images intended for Figures 2 through 8 appeared as Figures 1 through 7, respectively.Fig. 1KFP-1 promotes osteoblastic differentiation and mineralization in BMMSCs and MC3T3-E1 cells. BMMSCs and MC3T3-E1 cells were induced to differentiate into osteoblasts with varying concentrations of KFP-1.

title: The impoverishing effect of tobacco expenditures
creator: Elvina Merkaj, Drini Imami, Edvin Zhllima, Jeffrey Drope
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tobacco consumption is a major source of health and financial burden, yet evidence on its association with household poverty remains limited. This study examines how tobacco-related expenditures are associated with both the incidence and depth of poverty in Albania. Using nationally representative data from the Household Budget Survey, we estimate poverty indicators under three alternative definitions of household resources: observed expenditure, expenditure net of tobacco spending, and expenditure net of both tobacco and smoking-attributable healthcare costs.

title: Correction: Health anxiety by proxy differs in phenomenology between parents and dog owners
creator: Johanna Lass-Hennemann, Moritz N Braun, Charina C Lüder, Tanja Michael, Milena Weigel, Eva M Zenz, M Roxanne Sopp
description: t and affiliations now read: Johanna Lass-Hennemann1, Moritz N. Braun1, Charina C. Lüder1, Tanja Michael1,4, Milena Weigel2, Eva M. Zenz3 & M. Roxanne Sopp1,4 1Division of Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy, Department of Psychology, Saarland University, Campus Building A 1.3, Saarbrücken 66123, Germany. 2Independent Researcher, Bad Hersfeld, Germany. 3Independent Researcher, Leipzig, Germany.

title: Hierarchical multi-label structuring of Japanese SOAP clinical notes with large language models
creator: Ziheng Zhang, Minghui Tang, Feng Han, Hidenori Kitai, Kenji Hirata, Katsuhiko Ogasawara, Satoshi Konno, Kohsuke Kudo
description: Much clinically salient information in Japanese electronic medical records is recorded in SOAP (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) notes, which contain a lot of unstructured text preventing the further usage for analysis. Structuring such unstructured text is essential for secondary data use and clinical research.

title: Macrophage-driven pathological ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament: mechanistic insights and therapeutic opportunities
creator: Huohuo Xue, Tsutomu Endo, Ken Kadoya, Norimasa Iwasaki, M. Alaa Terkawi
description: Ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) is a chronic degenerative spinal condition in which bone gradually forms within the ligament, compressing the spinal cord and causing progressive neurological decline. While genetic predisposition and metabolic disturbances are well-recognized contributors, growing evidence points to macrophages as central players in shaping the tissue environment that drives pathological bone formation.

title: Prevention of altitude illness in adults: preparing people for travel to high altitude
creator: Sudeep Adhikari, Rudy Zimmer, Hermann Brugger, Nischal Bajracharya, Buddha Basnyat
description: nd signposting to sources of accurate and practical advice on prevention and recognition of altitude illness. Understand that tools exist to stratify altitude illness risk, and that a high level of baseline physical fitness and younger age are not protective against altitude illness.

title: Well-being differences and changes in people with somatic and psychiatric disorders or multimorbidities: modelling COVID-19 as a global natural experiment of stress vulnerability
creator: Till J Adam, Trevor Thompson, Fabiola H Peroz, Jan P Heisig, Paul Gellert, Enrique Alonso-Perez, Lara Bister, Lau Caspar Thygesen, Philippe Conus, Roland von Känel, Soraya Seedat, Denisa Manková, Daniel Guinart, Eduard Vieta, Mark J Millan, Diego De Leo, Michael Berk, Jess Fiedorowicz, Lin Yang, Jar
description: BackgroundSomatic and psychiatric illnesses and multimorbidities increase stress-vulnerability and decrease well-being.ObjectiveWe aimed to identify high-risk disorder profiles for lower well-being and well-being decline under stress, modelling COVID-19 as a natural experiment.MethodsThe global Collaborative Outcomes Study on Health and Functioning during Infection Times survey assessed the World Health Organization-Five Well-being Index (WHO-5) (0–100) retrospectively pre-pandemic and intra-pandemically.

title: Efficacy of Empirical Antibiotics in Community-Based Management of Uncomplicated Severe Acute Malnutrition in Children: Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Gomathi Ramaswamy, Sirisha Cheela, Kishore Yadav Jothula, Mounika Reddy, Raja S, Anand K Pyati, Patil Parag Parushuram, Priyanka Kotni, Khyati Tiwari, Sangeetha Sampath, Rahul Narang, Amy Schwartz
description: BackgroundAn estimated 17 million children have severe acute malnutrition (SAM) worldwide, with the majority residing in South Asia. Routine empirical antibiotics are prescribed for Community-based Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition (CSAM) to address presumed clinical/subclinical infections and improve nutritional recovery for children with uncomplicated SAM, but low prevalence of infection has been reported.

title: Developing a Shared Understanding of Humanism in Health Care Through Critical Review and Empirical Exploration: Protocol for a Modified e-Delphi Study
creator: Diane Guay, Annie Turcotte, Marie-Josée April, Véronique Foley, Jacinthe Beauchamp, Nicole Marquis, Michèle Héon-Lepage
description: BackgroundHumanism is central to the practice of health care professionals but remains poorly defined and inconsistently applied. Amid growing system pressures and dehumanization, this study aims to develop consensus-based conceptual and operational definitions of humanism to support education, evaluation, practice, and policy.

title: Effects of minerals and xylitol solution on human nasal epithelium: Water channels upregulation and potential anti-inflammatory properties
creator: Michelle Sabrina da Silva, Ana Laura Gaspar, Douglas Costa Morais, Fábio Ikedo, Flávia Cardoso Males, Gabriela Pacheco de Oliveira, Mariana Rodrigues Pinto, Rodrigo Torres Scabello, Stevin Zung, Edwin Tamashiro
description: Highlights•Xylitol-Mineral solution (XTM) is safe to the human nasal epithelium.•XTM does not induce pro- and inflammatory cytokines expression.•XTM preserves mucociliary transport.•XTM enhances aquaporin-3 expression, supporting potential epithelial hydration.•XTM downregulates inflammatory responses under LPS/TNF-alfa stimulation. Introduction Nasal mucosa is a pseudostratified tissue that filters inhaled air and provides defense against foreign agents, in addition to allowing the colonization of commensal microbiota.

title: Associations in Both Directions Between Internet Gaming Disorder and Suicidal Ideation and Attempts Among Chinese Adolescent Gamers: Two-Wave Prospective Cohort Study
creator: Pu Peng, Zhangming Chen, Silan Ren, Yudiao Liang, Youguo Tan, Xiaogang Chen, Jinsong Tang, Yanhui Liao, Stefano Brini, Badra Alghanami, Ali AL-Asadi, Lingfeng Gao
description: BackgroundInternet gaming disorder (IGD) has been associated with suicidal outcomes in adolescents, but most evidence is cross-sectional or has examined only whether IGD predicts later suicidality. Whether suicidal ideation and suicidal attempts are also associated with subsequent IGD remains unclear.

title: Serum zonulin levels and their association with inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis
creator: Ali B Roomi, Hussein Jawad Kadhim, Abbas Khairi Fadhil, Ibrahim Abdullah Hamzah
description: BackgroundMaintenance hemodialysis (HD) is accompanied by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and disturbances of the intestinal barrier.ObjectiveTo compare serum zonulin concentrations between patients receiving maintenance HD and healthy controls and to evaluate their associations with interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), and total antioxidant status (TAS).

title: NAE1-Dependent Protein Neddylation Preserves Endothelial Identity and Vascular Integrity
creator: Rachelle Nelson Zoni, Fatema Yeasmin Tanni, Chang Min Lee, Xiao Cheng, Jiyao Zhu, Vijaya Bhaskar Baki, MD Sadikul Islam, Jie Li, Huabo Su, Xinghui Sun
description: BackgroundEndothelial dysfunction is a central driver of cardiovascular and inflammatory diseases, yet the post-translational mechanisms that preserve endothelial homeostasis remain incompletely understood. Protein neddylation, the covalent conjugation of a ubiquitin-like modifier, regulates diverse cellular processes, yet its physiological role in the vascular endothelium remains unknown. This study investigated whether protein neddylation is required to preserve endothelial identity and vascular homeostasis.

title: RSV competes with the host for translational machinery without a host shutoff strategy
creator: Kyra Kerkhofs, Nicholas R Guydosh
description: RNA viruses often enhance ribosome recruitment to their own mRNAs through non-canonical sequence elements or by degrading host mRNA. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) produces mRNAs with host-like features, including 5’-cap and poly(A) tail. Therefore, the virus lacks an obvious mechanism to preferentially protect its own mRNAs or recruit ribosomes.

title: Evaluation of organ visualisation and biopsy quality during left-sided coelioscopy in rescued Northern boobooks (Ninox japonica)
creator: Jang-Hee Han, So-Eun Ryu, Hyeok-Won An, Hyeok Jin Son, Seung Yoon Ahn, Jinyoung Kim, Jun Won Park, Seong-Chan Yeon
description: Intra-vital diagnosis in wild raptors can be confounded by their stoic nature, often leading to cryptic morbidity. While coelioscopy offers a minimally invasive alternative, its performance regarding diagnostic utility and biopsy quality remains uncharacterised in small owls. Eight Northern boobooks (Ninox japonica) underwent diagnostic coelioscopy using a 2.7 mm rigid endoscope.

title: The role of inflammation on coronary microvascular dysfunction and potential therapeutic targets
creator: Wanqi Wang, Martina Magistri, John Beltrame, Noel Bairey Merz, Roxana Mehran, Vijay Kunadian
description: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a major underlying cause of myocardial ischaemia and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. It occurs both in the presence of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) and in patients with non-obstructive CAD. Emerging evidence highlights chronic inflammation as a key factor in CMD pathogenesis.

title: Measuring AI Progress in Drug Discovery: A Reproducible Leaderboard for the Tox21 Challenge
creator: Antonia Ebner, Christoph Bartmann, Sonja Topf, Günter Klambauer, Johannes Schimunek, Sohvi Luukkonen
description: Deep learning has fundamentally transformed fields such as computer vision and natural language processing since the early 2010s and has strongly influenced biomedical research. For drug discovery specifically, a key inflection pointakin to vision’s “ImageNet moment”arrived in 2015, when deep neural networks surpassed traditional approaches in the Tox21 Data Challenge.

title: Dynamics of Ligand Binding Sites and Chloride Penetration in a Bitter Taste GPCR
creator: Alon Rainish, Liel Sapir, Masha Y. Niv
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Taste perception strongly influences food choice, drug compliance, and dietary behavior. Bitter taste receptors belong to a subfamily of Family A GPCRs, while having unique features and deviations from conserved motifs. Recent cryo-EM structures revealed that the human bitter taste receptor TAS2R14 contains not only the canonical extracellular binding site, but also a novel intracellular site, raising questions about their interplay.

title: Can autonomous Agentic-AI systems accelerate drug discovery and development in the next decade?
creator: Navaneet Chaturvedi, Shafiul Haque, Vijay Kumar
description: The pharmaceutical industry is experiencing a profound transformation driven by rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), increasing research and development complexity, and the expiration of key patents. Agentic-AI systems, which enable autonomous reasoning, decision-making, and adaptive learning beyond traditional data-driven automation, represent a paradigm shift in this context.

title: Social media–based interventions to prevent adolescent nicotine use: a scoping review
creator: Lisa Melber, Elena Engel, Sascha Gell, Jaroslava Kaňková, Raffael Heiss
description: Despite growing concerns about adolescent nicotine use, the evidence regarding the outcomes of social media–based prevention efforts remains underexplored. This scoping review maps the scope, characteristics, and outcomes of (i) social media–based prevention interventions and (ii) educational interventions addressing adolescents’ interpretation of nicotine-related social media content.

title: Solution characterization of TrhW, a type 4 secretion system regulatory protein from the R27 plasmid
creator: Christina S. Rodriguez, Gerald F. Audette
description: Type IV secretion systems (T4SSs) are multiprotein nanomachines that mediate conjugative DNA transfer and contribute to the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes. The IncHI1 plasmid R27 encodes TrhW, a periplasmic T4SS-associated protein homologous to the F-plasmid proteins TraW and TrbC, which are expressed as separate polypeptides in many F-like systems but are fused into a single protein in IncHI1 plasmids.

title: Evidence-based design of a patient-specific quality assurance program through retrospective analysis of pretreatment and in vivo results
creator: Esther Decabooter, Sebastiaan M.J.J.G. Nijsten
description: Background and purposeAs radiotherapy techniques become increasingly complex, patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) must evolve to detect a broad spectrum of potential failure modes across the treatment chain. This study presents a extensive evaluation of a multi-modal PSQA program by assessing its ability to detect clinically relevant failure modes and quantifying its efficacy.

title: Cancer in Hispanic communities: Lower rates, larger gaps, and the work ahead
creator: Narjust Florez, Bárbara Segarra‐Vázquez
description: Lower overall cancer rates in Hispanic people hide excess hepatocellular, gastric, and cervical cancer, a rising burden in women, and widening gaps in coverage, language, and trust. Research conducted with Hispanic communities, rather than simply about them, is essential. Cancer is once again the leading cause of death among Hispanic people in the United States.

title: Unveiling the association of sirtuin1 (SIRT1) gene polymorphisms rs3758391 and rs12778366 with the risk, clinicopathological characteristics and susceptibility of breast cancer in Bangladeshi population
creator: Fariya Aboni, Md Rasel Khan Manik, Zimam Mahmud, Sonia Tamanna, Abdullah Al Saba, Farzana Ansari, Md. Zakir Hossain Howlader
description: Breast cancer (BC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Genetic variation in the SIRT1 (Sirtuin-1) gene has been implicated in cancer susceptibility; however, evidence regarding its association with breast cancer in the Bangladeshi population remains limited.

title: Antimycin A Improves Heat Tolerance in Creeping Bentgrass by Suppressing Nighttime Respiration and Reprogramming Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism
creator: Amir Abbas, Stephanie Rossi, Bingru Huang
description: High temperature causes an increase in plant respiration, which may contribute to growth decline under heat stress. The objectives of this study were to investigate whether suppressing heat‐elevated dark respiration with a respiration inhibitor, antimycin A (AA), could improve heat tolerance and alter carbon and nitrogen‐containing metabolite pools in creeping bentgrass ( Agrostis stolonifera “Penncross”).

title: Correction: STORM: spatial transcriptomics optimization by resolution via matrix factorization
creator: Unknown
description: tion ‘Integration of protein-protein interaction topology.’ The fifth sentence was removed: “The resulting interaction graph is inherently unsigned, since STRING scores represent confidence of functional associations aggregated from multiple evidence sources rather than explicit activating or inhibitory relationships.”) and the supplementary data file resupplied to the article.

title: An interim analysis of acute treatment adverse events and patient reported quality of life for functional imaging guided salivary gland sparing radiation therapy using diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging
creator: Katelyn Cahill, Catriona Hargrave, Kane Miller, Alexandria Leppien, Claudia Chapple, Jasmine Meaghan, Michelle Phan, Mark Denham, Patrick O'Connor, Alan Ho, David Hogan, Joanne Castelli, Zack Y. Shan, Myo Min
description: Background and purposeEvolving evidence suggests that regional sparing of the parotid gland during radiation therapy could reduce radiation-induced xerostomia in head and neck cancer. This interim analysis investigates the functional relationship between the diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) derived parotid gland biological at-risk volume (BRV) dose and acute adverse events, including patient-reported quality of life (QoL).

title: The southward expansion of Anopheles farauti (Diptera: Culicidae) in Australia: a genetic and ecological niche modeling investigation
creator: Fitsum Bekele, Luke Ambrose, Andrew F van den Hurk, Cassie C Jansen, Weng K Chow, Meredith Larney, Tristan P W Dennis, Nigel W Beebe, Danielle Tufts
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The mosquito Anopheles farauti Laveran (1902) is a coastal malaria vector with a wide distribution throughout the Southwest Pacific. This species shows strong population genetic structure across Australia, New Guinea, and the Solomon Archipelago. In Queensland, Australia, its southern range limit has been the 21° latitude but, in 2023, it was detected in mosquito surveys 300 km further south, at 23° latitude. Additional collections undertaken in 2024 suggested that a population of An. farauti had established at this new southern limit.

title: AI-bioinformatics synergy for precision medicine in brain diseases: integrating radiomics and multi-omics data
creator: Bekir Altas, Polymnia Georgiou, Anna Onisiforou
description: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and bioinformatics is reshaping the landscape of precision medicine in brain diseases, particularly in neurological diseases and brain tumors. Despite advances in both fields, the combined application of radiomics and multi-omics fusion remains underutilized, even though integrative frameworks are essential for addressing the complexity and heterogeneity of imaging and molecular data.

title: Special care dentistry: The quiet crisis at the margins of modern healthcare
creator: Yvonne M. Rooney, Zahra Shehabi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Special care dentistry (SCD) provides oral healthcare for adults who are unable to accept routine dental care due to physical, intellectual, medical, emotional, sensory, mental, or social impairments. In England, demand for SCD services is increasing in the context of population ageing, rising multimorbidity, improved tooth retention into later life, and persistent inequalities in access to National Health Service dental care.

title: Large Rabi Splitting Driven by Plasmon‐Enhanced Hybrid Anapole States in Si–Au–WSe2 Heterostructures
creator: Yanhui Deng, Mingyang Yu, Xizhen Xing, Chenxi Zhao, Tianyu Yang, Yujie Ma, Zhang‐Kai Zhou
description: Exciton–polaritons arising from strong light–matter coupling are key enablers of quantum coherent phenomena, whereas large Rabi splitting is critical for ensuring their robustness and stability. However, existing microcavity photonic modes rarely combine low radiative dissipation with strong field confinement, thereby limiting large splitting strong coupling, particularly in the few‐exciton regime.

title: Triple Space‐Polarization On–Off‐Key Modulation With AlN‐Based Tri‐Focal Metalens
creator: Zhi‐Yan Lin, Chen‐Yi Tsai, Bo‐Yi Chen, Huang‐Yu Wei, Hsiao‐Hsuan Yang, Yuh‐Jen Cheng, Hideto Miyake, Chia‐Yen Huang
description: We designed and demonstrated a tri‐focal metalens (TF‐lens) made of high‐temperature‐annealed AlN (HT‐AlN) on sapphire. The HTA‐AlN film possesses an ultrawide bandgap (E g = 6.2 eV), atomic‐level smoothness, and single‐crystalline quality, making it an exceptional candidate for a metasurface in visible spectral wavelengths.

title: Integrated Sensing and Communication in a Fiber‐Wireless System With Time‐Phase Synthesis Dimension Waveform
creator: Shengkun Chen, Zhenglin Tang, Weiqiang Lyu, Mengke Wang, Yaowen Zhang, Zhen Zeng, Lingjie Zhang, Heping Li, Zhiyao Zhang, Yong Liu
description: The convergence of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) across optical and wireless domains is a cornerstone for next‐generation networks, yet it is hindered by the fundamental incompatibility between fiber and wireless systems. Here, we introduce a unified fiber‐wireless ISAC system driven by a single microwave photonic platform.

title: Comparative evaluation of four household food‑waste composting systems for decentralized circular waste management
creator: Stanislava Voběrková, Eva Jansová, Martina Vršanská, Tomáš Do, Lenka Vaňková, Petra Martínez Barroso, Ivo Sedláček, Aleš Knoll, Ester Kovaříková, Magdalena Dária Vaverková
description: The study evaluated four household food waste composting systems using replicated trials (n = 3 per device) with standardized feedstock loads to compare temperature dynamics, physicochemical parameters, compost maturity, and microbiological safety. Although electric units automated mixing and heating, they did not achieve faster overall stabilization, and all devices produced semistabilized material requiring extended curing.

title: Applicator-dependent differences between TG-43 and a grid-based Boltzmann solver in iridium-192 high-dose-rate gynecological brachytherapy
creator: Bojan Pavičar, Andrej Milosavljević, Branko Predojević, Borislava Petrović
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo compare TG-43 and Acuros® BV dose estimates in iridium-192 (192Ir) high-dose-rate (HDR) gynecological brachytherapy across four applicator types and evaluate applicator-dependent differences. The novelty was the systematic comparison of multiple applicators within a single-institution workflow.Material and methodsThis retrospective dosimetric study included 40 patients and 121 treatment plans: tandem and ring (T&R, 34 plans), tandem and ovoid (T&O, 38 plans), segmented cylinder (SC, 23 plans), and universal multi-channel cylinder (UMC, 26 plans). All plans were generated in BrachyVision™ v.

title: Three-dimensional-printed template-assisted image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer: Technology, dosimetry, and clinical implementation
creator: Yuanjie Cao, Imashi Sandupama Wickramage, Chen Li, Qingxin Wang, Wenwen Zhang, Youheng Tan, Wenhui Yu, Ying Liu, Wei Wang, Qingsong Pang, Jie Chen
description: PurposeThree-dimensional (3D)-printed templates have emerged as practical tools to reduce geometric uncertainty and workflow variability in free-hand intracavitary/interstitial (IC/IS) brachytherapy for cervical cancer. This narrative review aimed to summarize contemporary evidence on 3D-printed templates and applicators, focusing on technology, dosimetry, clinical outcomes, and practical implementation within modern image-guided brachytherapy programs.

title: SMS text message reminders versus usual care for cervical screening attendance in London, UK: a retrospective secondary analysis of routinely collected data
creator: Beth Nichol, Josephine Ruwende, Jeff Powell Davies, Kaloyan Haralampiev, Christian Von Wagner, Aikaterini Grimani, Luke Vale, Ivo Vlaev
description: SummaryBackgroundPrevious randomised controlled trials have shown that general practitioner (GP)-endorsed text message reminders can increase cervical screening attendance. Following the implementation of these reminders across routine primary care services in London (UK), we aimed to assess their effect on likelihood of cervical screening attendance when implemented at scale.

title: Cross-tissue graph attention networks for semi-supervised gene expression prediction
creator: Shiyu Wang, Tianxing Hu, Mengyu He, Muran Qin, Yijuan Hu, Liang Zhao, Zhaohui Qin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High-throughput biotechnologies have significantly advanced precision medicine by enabling the exploitation of global gene expression patterns to enhance our understanding of disease etiology, progression, and treatment options. However, the tissue-specific nature of gene expression presents a challenge, particularly for less accessible tissues such as the brain, underscoring the need for computational methods to accurately impute gene expression in these critical but hard-to-reach tissues.

title: DecBin: Bayesian-optimized deep clustering for long-read metagenomic binning
creator: Yi-Heng Zhu, Xinchi Li, Zuo Liu, Jing Liu, Rui Ye, Wei Xue, Gaofei Jiang
description: Accurate metagenomic binning is essential for reconstructing microbial genomes, thereby facilitating the discovery of novel taxa, the identification of pathogens, and the characterization of antimicrobial resistance genes. Most existing methods are designed for assembled contigs and cannot be directly applied to raw long reads.

title: 3D analysis and evolution of prostate and tumor oxygenation using MRI-derived relative oxygen extraction fraction during MR-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy☆
creator: Thomas Berger, Ariane Lapierre, Perla Zidane, Hayder Aloraibi, Samy Horn, Angela Boros, Frederic Cervenansky, Benjamin Leporq, Olivier Beuf, William Henry Nailon, Olivier Chapet
description: Background/PurposeTumor hypoxia is a major cause of radioresistance, motivating the development of biomarkers related to tissue oxygen physiology that can be monitored throughout treatment. MRI-derived relative Oxygen Extraction Fraction (rOEF) is a non-invasive imaging biomarker related to tissue oxygen extraction. This study characterized the temporal evolution of rOEF during MR-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MRgSBRT) for prostate cancer.

title: Multimodality imaging for early detection of subacute myocardial rupture
creator: Giacomo Boi, Maria Francesca Marchetti, Riccardo Cau, Roberta Montisci, Sumit sohal, Alexandru Patrascu, Ahsan Aftab Khan, Michael ZL Zhu
description: ardiography showed inferior ST-segment elevation. Urgent coronary angiography revealed complete occlusion of the posterolateral branch of a dominant right coronary artery, with patency of a previously implanted left anterior descending artery stent (Video 1). The angiographic appearance did not allow definitive determination of the age of the occlusion.

title: PLPP1 inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling via enhancing Caveolin-1/β-catenin interaction and is negatively regulated by c-Myc in osteosarcoma
creator: Jiangbo Nie, Yang Zhou, Xinsheng Xie, Jinfa Wu, Weilai Tong, Zhiguo Shu, Shijiang Wang, Jiaming Liu, Feng Yang, Zhili Liu
description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents, characterized by rapid progression and poor prognosis. The molecular mechanisms underlying OS malignancy remain incompletely understood. Phospholipid phosphatase 1 (PLPP1) has recently been implicated in cancer biology, yet its role in OS is largely unknown.

title: Targeted delivery of siRNA against sodium-dependent phosphate co-transporter 2b (NPT2b) via functionalized mesoporous silica nanocarriers suppresses breast cancer cell growth
creator: Fatemeh Yazdi Samadi, Morteza Farab, Mahdieh Emadi, Marzieh Rad Niknam, Maryam Yousefi, Arash Minai-Tehrani
description: The sodium-dependent phosphate co-transporter 2b (NPT2b) plays an important role in maintaining phosphate homeostasis. In previous studies, we reported that high dietary inorganic phosphate consumption could increase NPT2b expression in mice while knockdown of NPT2b expression has been shown to reduce tumorigenesis. NPT2b has been found to be highly expressed in human breast cancer tissues.

title: Rare obstructive mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection with dual bidirectional drainage via a persistent left superior vena cava assessed prenatally with multimodal ultrasound: a case description
creator: Lin Chen, Dan Liu, Ying-Kun Guo, Xing-Yuan Zhang
description: onary venous obstruction (PVO), often requiring urgent neonatal surgery and leading to poor perinatal outcomes(1,2). Unlike classic multichannel mixed TAPVC, single common pulmonary venous trunk (CPVT) accompanied by bidirectional outflow is extremely rare, with only a few scattered reports describing this condition(3,4).

title: Precision resuscitation beyond neutral trials in cardiac arrest research
creator: Tae Nyoung Chung
description: tion. At the same time, several influential randomized trials across the cardiac arrest care continuum have reported neutral patient-centered outcomes. In the TTM2 trial, hypothermia at 33 °C did not reduce mortality or improve functional outcomes compared with targeted normothermia and early fever treatment [1].

title: Position-specific differences in match performance of elite U-17 soccer players using GPS-derived external load data: focus on forwards and defenders
creator: Chulsoon Choi, Hoseong Lee, Kwangjin Lee
description: [Purpose] The objective of this study was to investigate differences in match performance characteristics between forwards and defenders among elite U-17 soccer players using Global Positioning System (GPS)-derived data.[Methods] This study included 37 elite U-17 soccer players representing Gyeonggi Province. External load data collected during official matches were analyzed.

title: Long-term depressive symptoms trajectories following CBT delivered in primary care compared to usual treatment
creator: Maider Prieto-Vila, César González-Blanch, Rob Saunders, Joshua E. J. Buckman, Roger Muñoz-Navarro, Gabriel Esteller Collado, Sara Barrio-Martínez, Juan A. Moriana, Paloma Ruiz-Rodríguez, María Carpallo-González, Antonio Cano-Vindel
description: BackgroundThe course of depression is heterogeneous. The employed treatment is a key element in the impact of the course of depression over the time. However, there is currently a gap of knowledge about the trajectories per treatment and related baseline factors.

title: Trends of Survival and Brain Function Recovery in Sudden Cardiac Arrest Patients, 2013–2023
creator: Unknown

title: Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery
creator: Kwangjun Lee, Taejin Kwak, Wonil Park
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). [Purpose] A key pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is transactive response DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43, encoded by TARDBP) proteinopathy. Mutations in TARDBP and cellular stress can drive nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43. TDP-43 is an essential nuclear RNA-binding protein that regulates RNA metabolism, and cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation leads to aberrant splicing of essential neuronal transcripts including stathmin-2 (STMN2) and unc-13 homolog A (UNC13A).

title: Effects of plyometric training combined with tDCS on lower-limb muscle activation and cardiopulmonary function in male amateur soccer players: a randomized controlled trial
creator: Jeong-Il Kang, Dae-Joong Yang, Hyeong-Seok Lee
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to investigate the effects of combining transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) with plyometric training on lower-limb muscle activation and cardiorespiratory function in male amateur soccer players.[Methods] Thirty male amateur soccer players were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15).

title: SOX2-driven enhancer landscape defines the transcriptional architecture of retinogenesis
creator: Fuyun Bian, Kimiasadat Golestaneh, Emily Davis, Abdullah Khan, Brendan Nicholson, Marwa Daghsni, Keevon Flohr, Silvia Liu, Susana da Silva, Len Pennacchio, Issam Aldiri
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Retinal neurogenesis is mediated by the coordinated activities of a complex gene regulatory network (GRN) of transcription factors (TFs) in multipotent retinal progenitor cells (RPCs). How this GRN mechanistically guides neural competence remains poorly understood. In this study, we present integrated transcriptional, genetic and genomic analyses to uncover the regulatory mechanisms of SOX2, a key factor in establishing neural identity in RPCs. We show that SOX2 is preferentially enriched in the RPC-specific enhancer landscape associated with essential regulators of retinogenesis.

title: Latent profiles of body composition in older adults with hypertension: associations with physical fitness and differences in blood pressure and fasting plasma glucose
creator: Jae-Hoon Lee, Jaehee Lee, Min-Seong Ha
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to identify the body composition profiles of older adults with hypertension and examine their associations with physical fitness and cardiometabolic characteristics.[Methods] This cross-sectional study included 491 community-dwelling older adults with hypertension. Latent profile analysis was conducted using eight body composition indicators.

title: Withdrawn as duplicate: Sparse dimensionality reduction for analyzing single-cell-resolved interactions
creator: Niklas Brunn, Maren Hackenberg, Camila L Fullio, Tanja Vogel, Harald Binder, Yoshihiro Yamanishi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). (IMBI), Faculty of Medicine and Medical Center, University of Freiburg, Freiburg im Breisgau 79104, Germany; Freiburg Center for Data Analysis, Modeling and AI (FDMAI), University of Freiburg, Freiburg im Breisgau 79104, Germany. Maren Hackenberg, Institute of Medical Biometry and Statistics (IMBI), Faculty of Medicine and Medical Center, University of Freiburg, Freiburg im Breisgau 79104, Germany; Freiburg Center for Data Analysis, Modeling and AI (FDMAI), University of Freiburg, Freiburg im Breisgau 79104, Germany.

title: SUPERFICIAL VESSEL DENSITY, RETINAL NERVE FIBER LAYER THICKNESS, AND VISUAL FIELD LOSS IN PRIMARY OPEN-ANGLE AND PSEUDOEXFOLIATIVE GLAUCOMA
creator: Ante Prpić, Iva Ferček, Kim Kasa, Armin Kasumović, Ines Matoc, Idoia Goñi Guarro, Vedrana Vukić, Katia Novak-Lauš, Ivan Sabol, Zoran Vatavuk
description: SUMMARYThe aim was to examine peripapillary and macular superficial vessel density, peripapillary thickness of the nerve fiber layer, and inner thickness of the macula in eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and pseudoexfoliative glaucoma (PXG) depending on the visual field impairment. A total of 50 eyes were diagnosed as POAG and 50 as PXG.

title: Resistance to disinfection emerges in Salmonella Typhimurium following cyclic exposure to 3-(diethylamino)propylamine
creator: Alberto Fau, Jorge Andaluz-Arbe, Francisco de Borja Sánchez-Melendo, Diego Gómez-Lozano, Rafael Pagán, Diego García-Gonzalo, Daniel Berdejo
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Repeated lethal 3-(diethylamino)propylamine exposure selected tolerant variants.•Resistance outcomes varied among the three laboratory evolution protocols.•Obtained variants survived >1000-fold better after heat treatment.•Two obtained variants showed a two-fold increase in gentamicin MIC.•Resistance phenotypes varied according to the mutations identified.Keywords: Adaptive laboratory evolution, Disinfectant, Biocide, Resistant genetic variants, Thermotolerance, Antibiotic cross-resistance

Introduction

The European Union One Health 2024 Zoonoses report recorded > 1000 foodborne outbreaks related to Salmonella spp., with salmonellosis being the second most frequently reported food-borne gastrointestinal disease (EFSA and ECDC, 2025).

title: Glutamine Metabolism in Cardiac Hypertrophy
creator: Zhi-Guo Hu, Yao Yao, Yan Gong, Yu-Ting Yang
description: Cardiac hypertrophy represents a crucial adaptive response of the heart to various physiological and pathological stimuli, with metabolic reprogramming serving as the core mechanism driving this process. In recent years, the role of glutamine metabolism in cardiac hypertrophy has garnered increasing attention.

title: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis of the Diagnostic Efficacy of Transthoracic Echocardiography in the Classification of Patent Ductus Arteriosus
creator: Minxin Zhang, Chen Qian, Shuang Wang, Tianxing Fang, Bin Wang, Jinping Liu
description: Background:This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic efficacy of transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in classifying patent ductus arteriosus (PDA).Methods:A total of 616 patients diagnosed with PDA underwent TTE. TTE measurements were obtained using the parasternal short-axis view of the great arteries and the suprasternal fossa aortic long-axis view.

title: TEN-YEAR OUTCOMES AFTER ACUTE STEMI TREATED WITH PRIMARY PCI – THE ROLE OF ACUTE BIOMARKERS AND OTHER PARAMETERS IN PREDICTING CLINICAL SEVERITY AND PROGNOSIS
creator: Marko Mornar Jelavić, Zdravko Babić, Dorijan Babić, Diana Balenović, Ronald Lipovšćak, Hrvoje Pintarić
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SUMMARYThis rare prospective study investigated 10-year outcomes of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and evaluated the role of acute biomarkers and other parameters in predicting clinical severity and prognosis. We included 250 patients and analyzed their baseline (cardiovascular risk factors), laboratory (maximal CK/TnT, acute inflammatory (white blood cells (WBC), hs-CRP), and liver biomarkers (AST/LDH), glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)) and clinical severity parameters (length of hospital stay, in-hospital complications, coronary angiography, and echocardiography (LVEF)).

title: SKIN SURFACE TEMPERATURE CHANGES BEFORE AND AFTER MEDIAN NERVE DECOMPRESSION IN CARPAL TUNNEL SYNDROME
creator: Lucija Pavljak, Krešimir Bulić, Maksimilian Mrak, Anko Antabak
description: SUMMARYCarpal tunnel syndrome is the most common upper extremity compression neuropathy caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist. Along with motor and sensory fibers, sympathetic fibers also pass through the median nerve, playing an important role in the regulation of blood flow to the skin which interacts between the body interior and its environment.

title: The Role of Autoimmune Diseases in the Development of Aortic Aneurysms
creator: Jaroslav Michalek, Martin Petrek, Jana Petrkova
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aortic aneurysms are abnormal dilations of the aortic wall and represent a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. In many cases, especially when the thoracic aorta is involved, the first and only symptom is sudden death. While aortic aneurysms are traditionally associated with factors such as advanced age, hypertension, and atherosclerosis, growing evidence points to a critical role for autoimmune diseases in their pathogenesis.

title: A Multi Clone Kinetic Model for characterizing Chinese hamster ovary cell line variability
creator: Devi Sietaram, Pavlos Kotidis, Gary Finka, Alexei A Lapkin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper presents the Multi Clone Kinetic Model (MCKM), a novel generalized kinetic mechanistic model for fed-batch cultivations of diverse Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell lines, producing different recombinant monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Unlike traditional kinetic models requiring multiple cultures for one parameter regression, MCKM derives a complete set of 13 kinetic parameters from a single fed-batch cell line culture of 49 data points.

title: Characterization of S-glycosylated glycocins containing three disulfides
creator: Rachel M Martini, Chandrashekhar Padhi, Wilfred A van der Donk
description: Glycocins are a growing family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that are O- and/or S-glycosylated. Using a sequence similarity network of putative glycosyltransferases, the thg biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) was identified in the genome of Thermoanaerobacterium thermosaccharolyticum.

title: Short-termism in urban development: The commercial determinants of planetary health
creator: Daniel Black, Geoff Bates, Rosalie Callway, Kathy Pain, Ed Kirton-Darling
description: This article focuses on how short-termism impacts on the quality of urban development and, in turn, both population and planetary health. The first section of the paper clarifies key terms - short-termism, health, urban development and upstream - then summarises the context of urban development in the United Kingdom, and the evidence linking urban environments to population and planetary health.

title: Light‐Harvesting Protein LHCB4 Is Important for Stable Dimeric Organization of Photosystem II
creator: Tereza Vánská, Monika Opatíková, Roman Kouřil, Zuzana Kučerová, Václav Karlický, Iva Ilíková, Marek Rác, Pavel Roudnický, Vojtěch Chýlek, Petr Ilík
description: Light‐harvesting protein LHCB4 is a monomeric antenna of photosystem II (PSII) that connects the PSII core (C) with strongly (S) and moderately (M) bound LHCII trimers, forming the stable dimeric supercomplex C2S2M2. LHCB4 is known to stabilize LHCII attachment to the PSII core dimer (C2).

title: A comprehensive analysis of the prevalence and influencing factors of felid alphaherpesvirus-1 (FHV-1) in mainland China from 2017 to 2024
creator: Jiayu Shi, Huiling Zhang, Xinyuan Liu, Xueping Zhang, Hongyu Zhou, Tangjie Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ImportanceFelid alphaherpesvirus 1 (FHV-1) is a common cause of feline upper respiratory disease, but prevalence estimates from mainland China are fragmented.ObjectivesTo estimate pooled FHV-1 prevalence and evaluate factors associated with between-study variation in mainland China from 2017 through 2024.Data ResourcesPubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the Chinese Journal Service Platform were searched; reference lists were also screened.

title: Clinical Characteristics of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Korean Children: An 11-Year Multicenter Retrospective Study
creator: Young Hwa Lee, Yoon Lee, Young June Choe, Jue Seong Lee, Young Yoo, Hyeon-Jong Yang, Jeong-Won Oh, Jinseop Kim, Eunseo Jo, Sujin Choi, Hyun Jung Kim, Lorenzo Bertizzolo
description: BackgroundRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in children. This study investigates the clinical characteristics, factors descriptively associated with severity, and shifts in age distribution of RSV infection in Korean children over an 11-year period.

title: A Notch signaling pathway-related gene signature: Characterizing the immune microenvironment and predicting prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Qingmiao Shi, Shuwen Jiang, Yifan Zeng, Xin Yuan, Yaqi Zhang, Qingfei Chu, Chen Xue, Lanjuan Li
description: Background and ObjectivesPrior studies have highlighted an escalating global burden of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The Notch signaling pathway regulates the initiation and development of HCC and determines the HCC prognosis.MethodsThe expression data of genes related to the Notch signaling pathway were acquired from public databases.

title: Long-term Immunogenicity and Safety Profile of the Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccine in Korean Older Adults: A Sub-analysis of a Phase 3 Trial
creator: Seong-Beom Park, Suryaprakash Mishra, Sang-Kyu Shin, Stebin Xavier, Giulia Zigon, Manuel Zocco, Marie Van Der Wielen, Dong-Gun Lee, on behalf of the AReSVi-006 study group
description: BackgroundRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) poses substantial health risks to elderly adults and adults with certain underlying conditions. In a multi-country phase 3 trial (AReSVi-006), the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine has shown high efficacy against RSV disease. This post-hoc sub-analysis assessed immunogenicity, immunopersistence up to 24 months, and safety of a single dose of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in the Korean cohort.

title: Atopic Dermatitis and Sleep Disorders
creator: Genlong Bai, Xinyi Shao, Yi Ou, Jin Chen, Zhaofu Tan, Aijun Chen, Jingbo Zhang
description: PurposeAtopic dermatitis (AD) is a common inflammatory skin disease affecting 129 million people worldwide and is characterized by recurrent eczema, severe pruritus, and skin barrier damage. Previous studies on AD-sleep disorder associations were limited by small sample sizes or single-center designs, lacking large-scale epidemiological evidence.

title: Novel supplementation of Fe3O4-doped green carbonized nanoparticles on hydrogenases genes and microbial biodiversity for enhancing biohydrogen yield in dark fermentation microbial electrohydrogenesis cells
creator: Hikmatullah Ahmadi, Anam Jalil, Sohail Khan, Irfan Ali Phulpoto, Zhang Chengyu, Zhisheng Yu
description: Achieving high-purity biohydrogen (Bio-H₂) production necessitates the suppression of hydrogenotrophic methanogens, as their activity can impede hydrogen yield. Various inoculum pretreatments have been employed to suppress methane-producing microorganisms; however, these methods can negatively impact the enzymatic activity of hydrogen-producing microorganisms, thereby reducing hydrogen production.

title: Efficacy of Starting Very-Low-Dose Cow’s Milk Intake in Children Aged 1–12 Years With Severe Cow’s Milk Allergy: A Retrospective Study
creator: Kosei Yamashita, Takanori Imai, Sawa Seki, Toshiyuki Takagi, Megumi Okawa, Aiko Honda, Chihiro Kunigami, Yuki Okada, Mayu Maeda, Taro Kamiya
description: PurposeTo avoid the complete elimination of cow’s milk (CM) from the diet, we introduced a very-low-dose (VLD) oral food challenge (OFC) as part of an OFC-based stepwise ingestion protocol in patients with severe CM allergy in 2019, when the OFC protocol at our center was revised.

title: Organelle Crosstalk: Mitochondria and Endoplasmic Reticulum in Macular Degeneration
creator: Iffat Alam, Ayeshah Hussain, Devendra K. Agrawal
description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss characterized by progressive retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction, mitochondrial damage, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. While mitochondrial dysfunction is a known contributor to AMD, the contribution of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) has not been fully explored.

title: Identification and validation of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)-associated targets for monascin from the extracts of Monascus purpureus-fermented rice: Compound preparation, high-throughput genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis
creator: Xilinqiqige Bao, Hanqing Li, Jiayin Xu, Xiaoqing Liu, Runa A, Jianming Chen, Fengzheng Chen, Nan Ya, Rigula Sa
description: Despite the remarkable bioactivities exhibited by monascin against several tumors, its therapeutic targets remain unexplored. In this study, our objective is to identify therapeutic targets based on the antitumor activity of monascin against lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) A549 cells. The compound monascin was derived from extracts of Monascus purpureus-fermented rice.

title: A SCOPING REVIEW PROTOCOL ON THE EFFECT OF GYNAECOLOGICAL CANCERS: THEIR DIAGNOSES AND MANAGEMENT ON THE MENTAL HEALTH OF AFFECTED WOMEN IN SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA
creator: OC Idowu, OS Oyerinde, AA Odukogbe, OA Awolude, CC Asuzu, IO Morhason-Bello, IF Adewole
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction:Mental health describes an individual's emotional, psychological, and social well-being. The diagnosis of precancers and cancers may result in different mental health manifestations. This review will examine the existing evidence on the effects of diagnosis, management, and prognosis of the four common gynaecological malignancies (ovarian, endometrial, cervical cancer, and endometrial trophoblastic neoplasia) and two precursor lesions (premalignant lesions of the cervix and hydatidiform mole) on the mental health of affected women in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).Materials & Methods:Electronic databases will be thoroughly searched,

creator: The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific
description: burden of premature deaths attributed to air pollution. In May, 2026, the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific published its first comprehensive overview of air-quality standards across the region. Although half of countries have established standards for at least one pollutant, none have national standards fully aligned with WHO global air-quality guidelines. An estimated 1.

title: BREASTFEEDING AND ACUTE RESPIRATORY INFECTION (ARI) IN INFANTS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW IN NIGERIA
creator: A George, S Bonne, EN Ekpenyong, EN Edem, S Ajayi
description: Background:Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) significantly contribute to infant morbidity and mortality worldwide, especially in developing countries like Nigeria, where factors such as inadequate nutrition, poor environmental conditions, and partial immunization increase their incidence, while exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) offers immune protection that can reduce their incidence and severity.

title: Ancient mitochondrial DNA analysis of human remains in the era of next- generation sequencing
creator: Dina W. Ibrahim, Haidan Mostafa El-Shorbagy, Ismail A. Abdelhamid, Yehia Z. Gad
description: The analysis of ancient DNA (aDNA) has become important in recent years, providing new insights on human evolution and population history. Since the emergence of ancient DNA analysis in the mid-eighties, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) analysis has been an essential tool in paleogenomic research.

title: Landscape of cancer genomics and precision oncology in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia
creator: Hideaki Bando, Hirokazu Okayama, Yoon Jung Chang, Jinpu Yu, Sean M. Grimmond, Sun-Young Kong, Xin Hu, Nikolajs Zeps, Ji-Youn Han, Jong-Il Kim, Kyosuke Seguchi, Masataka Amisaki, Yasutoshi Sakamoto, Takao Fujisawa, Riu Yamashita, Kazuto Kato, Koji Kono, Amber Johns, Takayuki Yoshino
description: SummaryPrecision oncology has expanded rapidly across the Asia–Pacific region, yet implementation remains heterogeneous because of differences in health-system organisation, reimbursement, molecular tumour board infrastructure, workforce capacity, and data integration. This structured narrative review with expert consultation compares precision oncology ecosystems in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia to identify common challenges and implementation strategies across the patient pathway.

title: PERCEPTION OF HEALTH CARE WORKERS ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED MALARIA DIAGNOSIS IN SOUTHWESTERN NIGERIA
creator: OS Michael, E Bukoye, P Whiley, N Idusuyi, P Casserly, D Ademola, AO Coker
description: Background :Effective control of malaria is anchored on accurate diagnosis. Conventional Methods of diagnosis include microscopy, and malaria rapid diagnosis. Many factors, particularly human error, diagnostic inaccuracies of microscopy due to human errors. The study reports the results of an online survey designed to assess the perception of health workers on artificial intelligence methods in the diagnosis of malaria.

title: A primary isolated heart model of Takotsubo syndrome for mechanistic investigation and preclinical therapeutic testing
creator: Amirali Nejat, Ermir Zulfaj, Yalda Kakaei, Mana Kalani, Tetiana Pylova, Maryna Krasnikova, Ahmed Elmahdi, Sandeep Jha, Björn Redfors, Elmir Omerovic, Francesco Paneni
description: AimsCurrent experimental models of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) do not readily distinguish intrinsic myocardial responses from systemic neurohumoral influences. We sought to establish and comprehensively characterize a primary isolated heart TTS model, in which the complete TTS-like phenotype is induced entirely within a Langendorff-perfused rat heart, enabling mechanistic investigation and preclinical therapeutic testing under controlled conditions.

title: Temporal Trends of Stillbirth in Brazil Disaggregated by Maternal and Gestational Age
creator: Maria Isabel do Nascimento, Lara Miranda Marchesi, Wender Emiliano Soares, Jenaine Rosa Godinho Emiliano, Maria Auxiliadora Nogueira Saad, Glaucimara Gonzaga Nunes Hacar, Gabriel Eijiro Chiracava
description: Objective:Stillbirth is a neglected problem that needs to be given a greater visibility, especially in developing countries. This study aimed to describe temporal trends of stillbirth rates disaggregated by maternal and gestational age.Materials and methods:This is an ecological study conducted in Brazil.

title: Association Between Sociodemographic Characteristics and Assisted Childbirth by Qualified Personnel in Madagascar
creator: Hery Sylvestre Bemanana
description: Objective:This study aims to analyze the association between the likelihood of giving birth in a healthcare facility and various sociodemographic characteristics in Madagascar.Materials and methods:This study utilized data from the 2021 Madagascar Demographic and Health Survey which included a representative sample of women of reproductive age (15–49 years).

title: Topology-guided dual-masked contrastive learning for weakly supervised cell-type annotation in single-cell multi-omics
creator: Yi Zhang, Longneng Ran, Yu Liang, Xiaohua Wang, Hanyan Wei
description: Single-cell multi-omics technologies provide complementary views of cellular states, but are challenged by pervasive feature sparsity, pronounced cross-modality heterogeneity, and a critical shortage of labeled cells, hindering accurate cell-type annotation. We propose dual-masked contrastive learning (DMCL), a topology-guided weakly supervised cross-modal representation learning framework that addresses these challenges within a unified architecture.

title: VeloHARMO: a deep learning framework for mRNA coding sequence generation and design via translation velocity harmonization
creator: Bian Bian, Jichen Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Yutaka Saito
description: Heterologous gene expression often results in suboptimal protein yield or activity, potentially influenced by differences in translation dynamics between native and host organisms. Conventional mRNA design approaches based on codon usage frequency can improve expression efficiency. However, codon usage frequency alone does not necessarily reflect codon-level translation velocity.

title: Microbial Enzymes in Industrial Biotechnology: Sources, Production, and Significant Applications of Lipases
creator: Nisha Sharma, Yogesh K Ahlawat, Nattan Stalin, Sajid Mehmood, Sonia Morya, Anurag Malik, Malathi H, Jayshree Nellore, Deepak Bhanot
description: The variety of microorganisms represents the most prevalent sources utilized within diverse industries and research fields. Enzymes with microorganisms are applied in the use of industrial biotechnology. Since the dawn of civilization, there are techniques like extraction and fermentation that use plant or bacterial enzymes as well as other byproducts.

title: A Rare Encounter: Incidental Ectopic Origin of the Right Pulmonary Artery in an Adult
creator: Rupali Jain, Maruti Kumaran, Achala Donuru
description: Ectopic origin of the right pulmonary artery (RPA) from the aorta is a rare congenital anomaly typically found in infants. We report an adult female presenting with shortness of breath diagnosed incidentally with ectopic RPA via computed tomography angiography. This case underscores the need to consider rare congenital anomalies in adults presenting with unexplained pulmonary symptoms.

title: Exercise-Induced Activation of IGF-1/mTOR Signaling and Hippocampal BDNF/PGC-1α Expression Reverses Age-Related Motor Decline
creator: Taewan Kim, Jinkyung Cho, Yoonhwan Kim, Sang Koo Woo, Donghyun Kim
description: PurposeAging is associated with a progressive decline in skeletal muscle function and motor coordination, contributing to reduced mobility and quality of life. While exercise is a well-established intervention to counteract age-related deterioration, the underlying molecular mechanisms in both muscle and the brain remain incompletely understood.

title: Adoption of a novel medium for the industrial (3000 L) production of Serendipita indica employing a nutrient limitation strategy using insoluble carbon and phosphate sources
creator: Jubair Al Rashid, Md Abuhena, Md Dilshad Karim, Lutfur Rahman, Jingjing Wang, Zhiyong Huang
description: The use of the endophytic fungus Serendipita indica has rapidly increased due to its wide range of host species, ability to foster plant-growth, and ability to confer tolerance to a number of stresses. However, its industrial-scale production is still in its infancy due to its low-biomass yield and prolonged cultivation time.

title: 产后访视能力的研究进展
creator: Guoqing WANG, Xiaoyu LI, Yimei XIE, Wenjie GONG, 柳 宋
description: 产后访视是基层妇幼保健人员在产妇出院后1周内到其家中进行的保健服务。然而，中国对此缺乏具体工作细则和标准，难以有效评估产后访视人员能力，提高其服务质量。本文采用主题词加自由词相结合的方式检索中英文数据库，根据纳入和排除标准对检索文献进行筛选，纳入24篇文献，提取并归纳产后访视能力及相关要求。产后访视能力内容可归纳为健康评估、健康教育和沟通协调3个维度。访视人员能够完成基本的产妇和新生儿的身体检查及健康宣教，但在提供更具专业性的保健服务时存在一定的不足。访视人员个人特征、技术能力及培训等影响产后访视服务的交付效果。访视能力提升策略包括教学形式改革、家访技能培训、规范访视程序。目前缺乏全面评估产后访视能力的方法。Keywords: 产后访视, 能力, 影响因素, 提升策略, 评估方法, 妇幼保健 产后访视作为国家基本公共卫生服务中孕产妇健康管理服务的重要内容，是孕期健康管理和住院分娩之后的延伸服务，主要由产妇居住地社区卫生服务中心(站)/乡镇卫生院的基层妇幼保健人员在产妇分娩出院后1周内到产妇家中对其及新生儿进行面对面的保健服务，以完成随访、观察、体格检查和健康指导等服务[1]。高水平、高质量的产后访视，可有效降低产妇及新生儿的死亡率，提高家庭对相关疾病的管理及转诊能力[2]，并提高母乳喂养成功率[3-4]，有效地保障产妇和新生儿的身心健康，是基层妇幼保健的重点工作之一。然而，当前中国缺乏产后访视工作的具体细则，也未制订相应的工作标准，即负责产后访视的保健人员应该具备何种能力及能力水平。产后访视人员能力参差不齐，难以满足产妇及新生儿的保健需求，亟须采取有效的措施提高产后访视能力。因此，本文旨在通过文献回顾，系统阐述产后访视能力的要素、含义、现状、影响因素、提升策略及评估方法，以期为后续相关研究和产后访视能力的提升提供参考。 文献检索及结果 研究者对中国知网、万方、Web of Science、Cochrane Library、PubMed、Embase、Ovid共7个数据库进行检索，检索范围为自建库至2023年7月1日发表的国内外关于产后访视能力文献。中文检索词为“围产期”“围生期”“产后”“孕产妇”“分娩后”“妊娠”“妇女”“产褥期”“新生儿”“婴幼儿”“访视”“家访”“家庭随访”“能力”“技能”“胜任力”“质量”等。英文检索词为“competence”“skill”“home visit”和“postpartum period”等。 文献纳入标准：1)围绕产后访视能力开展的研究；2)经过同行评议的原始研究(包括实证研究、考核、培训、模型框架类研究、定性访谈等)；3)以英文或中文发表的研究。排除标准：1)未在产后42 d内开展访视活动；2)产后访视人员在家访时仅交付研究人员指定的保健服务，而非常规保健服务。本研究经筛选最终得到24篇有效文献，包括11篇中文文献、13篇英文文献。 产后访视能力要素 产后访视能力可以归纳为健康评估、健康教育和沟通协调3个维度。这些能力包含评估产妇及新生儿的身心健康状态，针对性地开展健康教育，完成产后访视安排，处理产后访视信息等(表1)。 表1产后访视能力要求Table 1 Postpartum visit competence requirements能力产后访视内容具体要求健康评估评估产妇的身体和心理健康状态 询问过敏史、用药史、目前食欲、饮食、睡眠等一般健康状况 测量体温、血压，触诊乳房、子宫底下降程度、腹直肌分离程度，询问恶露情况、腹部或侧切伤口；筛查产妇心理健康状态 识别有无异常情况并转诊 评估新生儿的身体健康状态和养育情况 询问喂养方式、24 h喂养次数、喂养量、大便及体重变化情况 测量体重和体温，检查脐带脱落情况、黄疸情况 识别有无异常情况并转诊 健康教育基于产妇的身体和心理健康状态进行健康教育指导产褥期卫生、产后恢复、产后营养搭配、产后避孕基于新生儿的身体健康状态和养育情况进行健康教育 指导母婴互动、新生儿喂养技能、新生儿发育特点、新生儿正常行为、新生儿 免疫接种 开展家庭暴力评估与处理、婴儿虐待评估与处理
